A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
proton capture chains are active in the interior of red giants in all globular clusters.
the [Mg] and [He] abundances of cluster giants, and thus their horizontal-branch morphology, may depend on the extent of deep mixing within the stars.

proton capture chains in globular clusters are not only important for explaining the observed abundance differences between stars of different masses in a cluster, but also for explaining the different horizontal-branch morphologies of the various clusters.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the [O/Na/Al/Mg] ratios within NGC 7006 red giants are consistent with the idea that proton-capture–processing has occurred within the interiors of these stars.
the [O/Na/Al] abundances of globular cluster giants provide a sensitive probe of the amount of proton capture–processed material that is mixed into the envelopes.
the [Mg/H] ratio is a much better indicator of the degree of deep mixing within cluster giants than is the [Mg/Mn] ratio.
